rules: 1 all-in crypto pick per day, 100% deployed
Spot crypto only (BTC, ETH, SOL, and other liquid coins on Robinhood)
Rotate each 6:45am CT run — sell yesterday, buy today's best
Hard stop at entry; leverage conviction, protect downside

positions.name: Ethereum
positions.catalyst: ETH owns the only structurally IMPROVING institutional flow story in the majors. U.S. spot Ether ETFs are taking net inflows ($18.4M on Jul 10, BlackRock $16.2M of it) while Bitcoin's ETF complex is still ~-$5.4B net YTD in 2026 — the flow arrow points opposite directions. The staking-ETF pipeline is the live, ETH-only catalyst: the SEC/CFTC joint interpretive release (Mar 17, 2026) classified staking rewards as non-securities, Grayscale (ETHE) and BlackRock (ETHB, launched Mar 12 with $107M seed) are already live, and pending staking amendments from Fidelity, Franklin Templeton, Invesco, 21Shares and VanEck are queued for approval — each one converts ETH from a zero-yield asset into a ~2.6-3.0% yielding one inside a regulated wrapper. Second, today's binary is macro, not crypto-specific: June CPI prints 8:30am ET Jul 14 and Fed Chair Warsh testifies House today / Senate Wed. On a day whose outcome is set by an inflation number, the correct trade is the LIQUID MAJOR with the best relative strength — not the highest-beta alt. BlackRock's commentary during the week doubles as a health check on ETH ETF demand.
positions.driver: ETH was the ONLY major that went up over the last 24h while the tape was red. Measured on our own dashboard feed 24h-to-24h (Jul 13 11:53Z -> Jul 14 11:53Z): ETH +0.88% ($1,781.40 -> $1,797.04), BTC -0.10% ($62,867.22 -> $62,802.91), XRP -0.60% ($1.0779 -> $1.0714), SOL -1.34% ($76.39 -> $75.37). That is a clean rotation of the relative-strength baton: yesterday SOL was the best relative performer in a flush and it FAILED — it did not lead the bounce, it led the bleed, so the thesis is invalidated and we do not repeat it. ETH absorbed the oil-spike/Iran risk-off and the renewed inflation scare and still closed the 24h green, holding the $1,700-$1,800 range it has defended all month. Into a CPI print with a genuinely two-sided outcome, that is exactly the asymmetry we want: ETH sits near the LOWER half of a well-defined range (defined $1,700 shelf below = a real stop reference, $1,800 breakout trigger just overhead), it carries roughly half SOL's beta so a bad CPI hurts less, and a benign CPI puts it through $1,800 with the staking-ETF flow bid behind it. Runners-up rejected: SOL (yesterday's pick) is now the WORST 24h major and its CLARITY-Act catalyst has slipped again — the merged bill is only 'expected as soon as this week' with floor action pushed to the week of Jul 20, and delay hits high-beta alts hardest; BTC is flat, its ETF complex is still bleeding, and it is the most directly exposed to the oil/geopolitics risk-off; XRP is red with no fresh catalyst. Entry = dashboard live feed (asOf 2026-07-14T11:53:15Z).
positions.risks: The single biggest risk is the CPI print itself (8:30am ET today) — a hot June number revives the 'renewed inflation fears' that knocked crypto down 3% yesterday, and ETH will not be spared; the whole complex is trading as a high-beta risk asset tied to the dollar, Treasury yields and NAS100, not on crypto-native fundamentals. Warsh's first semiannual testimony (House today, Senate Wed) is an untested variable and the single largest swing factor for digital-asset liquidity — a hawkish long-run-rates message drains it. ETH's relative-strength edge is thin (~1pp over BTC) and one day old, which is the same fragile signal that just failed us on SOL. The staking-ETF catalyst is a slow institutional drip, not a next-24h event: net yield to holders after issuer cuts is a modest 2-3%, Citi just cut its 12-month ETH target from $3,175 to $2,240 citing weak flows, and ETH is still far below its 2024 ETF-launch expectations. $1,800 has been repeated overhead resistance and a rejection there is the base case if CPI is anything other than benign. Oil/Iran geopolitics remain live 24/7. Hard stop $1,653.28 (-8%).
